statement: For REPDF C9, an exhaustive single-byte-substitution search per damaged Flate stream (candidates restricted to bytes before zlib's error point when it errors, as in Barral et al.), accepting candidates that inflate cleanly and pass Adler-32 and then filtering by PDF secondary oracles (decoded length vs /Length1, TrueType table checksums, content-stream tokenisation), restores the original stream uniquely and correctly for at least 90% of the 1442 damaged streams, with no unique-but-wrong corrections.
metric: Per damaged stream: unique-and-correct / ambiguous / none / unique-but-wrong, against the original stream bytes; CPU seconds per stream. Report with and without the secondary oracles, to measure Adler-32-only ambiguity.
baseline: Prefix salvage (decode until error), and the stream-level output of qpdf and mutool on the same files.
data: REPDF C9 files and originals (SRC-0002, commit e547d4d); per-stream ground truth from research/staging/scoping-compression/experiments/results/flate_c9_probe.csv (OBS-0300).
notes: Seeds a W1 spec. Each damaged stream has exactly one changed byte (OBS-0300), so the search is at most 255 x compressed length inflations per stream (median length 9547 bytes).
refute_if: Unique-and-correct below 70% of damaged streams, or at least one unique-but-wrong correction, or median CPU time above 60 s per stream on one core.

statement: Given the position of the damaged byte, Brown-2013-style intra-block resynchronization (skip a small window after the damage, decode from every candidate bit offset until the segmentations converge, carry the unknown history as co-indexed symbols so history-dependent bytes stay 'unknown') recovers verbatim a median of at least 50% of the post-damage decoded bytes of single-block C9 streams, where block-level resync recovers 0%, and emits no byte as known that differs from the original.
metric: Per damaged single-block stream: verbatim post-damage fraction, unknown fraction, count of bytes emitted as known but wrong (must be 0), convergence distance in bytes.
baseline: Prefix salvage; block-level resync (next intact block).
data: The 853 damaged C9 streams that are single-block (OBS-0301), with originals.
notes: Localisation is given (oracle) in this first test; combining it with GAP-150 localisation is a second step. Mark Adler's two-dictionary check (CLM-0337) is a cheap way to verify the 'no known-but-wrong byte' property.
refute_if: Median verbatim post-damage fraction below 20%, or any byte emitted as known that differs from the original.

statement: A per-file toolpath selector trained on fidelity labels (agreement with the known original, not 'opens in a viewer') closes at least half of the gap between the single best toolpath and the per-file oracle (virtual best) on held-out damaged PDFs, and with a reject threshold escalates at most 10% of files while keeping the fabrication rate under the pre-registered ceiling.
metric: Share of the single-best/virtual-best gap closed on the primary endpoint; fabrication rate of auto-accepted files; escalation rate.
baseline: Single best toolpath; the fixed Resave/TemplateAssemble order of the current design.
data: Needs several toolpaths run on a damaged corpus with known originals (REPDF for development only; the held-out suite for the claim).
notes: Answers RQ5 / gentle-gosling s2. Candidate threshold methods: Chow's reject rule (SRC-0331), learning to defer (SRC-0330); candidate escalation design: guided data repair (SRC-0329).
refute_if: Selector closes less than 25% of the single-best/virtual-best gap, or needs to escalate more than 30% of files to meet the fabrication ceiling.
